2023_055_nbs_elementary.paragraph: A packet of NBS (NBS Troy) furniture quotations numbered 360054 through 360063, quoted 03/14/23 and 03/15/23 under project 230329 for customer T00031, covering flexible-seating purchases for named classrooms at Troy School District elementary buildings. Pricing is drawn from the E&I contract for Smith System and PEPPM plus additional dealer discounting for Fomcore, on NET 10 DAYS terms with a purchase order and 40% deposit required before order placement. The largest of the quotations is 360058 for Leonard Elementary, a grand total of $10,525.78 that includes a $2,297.74 double whiteboard straight mobile cabinet.

2023_056_m021423bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of February 14, 2023, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. before roughly 75 audience members and adjourned at 8:35 p.m. The Board recognized Fall 2022 All-State athletes, honored eight LitCon presenters, and adopted resolution 23-017 declaring February Principal Appreciation Month. Its most consequential action was resolution 23-020 awarding the Site Work Paving Program bid to Nagle Paving, at an amount printed as $2,2,46,617.00 inclusive of a 6% contingency, payable from the Building Site and Sinking Fund and Capital Projects Fund.
2023_056_m021423bdmtg.page:
**Meeting** \ Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, February 14, 2023, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; the meeting adjourned at 8:35 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

**Attendance** \ In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Fulcher, Haezebrouck and West. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended.

**Recognitions** \ Mr. Tim Fulcher, Director of Athletics, recognized Fall 2022 All-State athletes: Daniel Watkins, Carter Cusmano, John Palomino and Nick Worrell (Boys' Soccer); Olivia Hemmila, Ava Weeks and Riley Hayden (Girls' Golf); Derek Blackwell, Derrick Kim, Nish Palepu, Srihari Ananthalwan and Rushil Kagithala (Boys' Tennis); Vishvaa Ravishankar (Boys' Cross Country); and Darius Whiteside (Boys' Football). The Mission Moment honored the 8 teachers who represented the District at LitCon, the National Reading Recovery/Early Literacy Conference: Karen Bush and Holly Gordon, Ashley Pellosmaa and Sue Reid of Wattles, and classroom teachers Sara Provost, Alyssa Favot, Kristen Marcaccio and Erin Miller.

**Actions**

| No. | Item | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23-017 | Resolution recognizing February as Principal Appreciation Month | Mrs. Anne / Dr. Wilson | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-018 | Consent agenda items A-F | Mr. Hauff / Mrs. Alic | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-019 | Adoption of the 2023-2024 High School Course Description Book | Dr. Wilson / Mrs. Anne | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 23-020 | Site Work Paving Program bid to Nagle Paving | Dr. Philippart / Mr. Haupt | Yes 7, No 0 |

**Consent agenda (23-018)** \ Minutes of the January 10, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the January 17, 2023 Board of Education Organizational & Regular Meeting; Treasurer's Report - December 2022; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; and OCSBA Legislative Priorities and Bylaw Amendments.

**Curriculum** \ Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, and Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, presented recommended changes to the 2023-2024 High School Course Catalogue by PowerPoint. Board discussion covered the workshop model of teaching, changes in ELA and Chemistry courses, team sports, and co-ed physical education classes.

**Business** \ The Site Work Paving Program bid was awarded to Nagle Paving in an amount printed in the minutes as $2,2,46,617.00 inclusive of a 6% contingency, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund and Capital Projects Fund.

**Public communication** \ Mrs. Tracy Owens, TSD parent, spoke on proposed High School Course Catalogue changes and their impact on students; Mrs. Eleni Dilis, TSD parent, spoke about honors classes being taken away and asked that parents be given a chance to share their thoughts. No non-agenda public comment was offered.

**Student representatives** \ Alexi Papadelis (Troy College and Career High School, moved earlier in the agenda), Nish Palepu (Troy High School), Sara Ali (Athens High School) and Yara Mashal (International Academy-East).

**Announcements** \ Board Workshop March 7 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building; Board Winter Retreat Saturday, March 11 at 9:00 a.m. at the Administration Building; next Board Meeting March 21 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.
2023_056_m021423bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, for the Board Meeting of February 14, 2023, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Fulcher, Haezebrouck and West. There were approximately 75 members of the audience.

**Recognition - All-State Athletes Fall 2022.** Mr. Tim Fulcher, Director of Athletics, recognized students named All-State Athletes in their respective sports: Daniel Watkins (Boys' Soccer), Olivia Hemmila (Girls' Golf), Ava Weeks (Girls' Golf), Carter Cusmano (Boys' Soccer), John Palomino (Boys' Soccer), Nick Worrell (Boys' Soccer), Derek Blackwell (Boys' Tennis), Derrick Kim (Boys' Tennis), Nish Palepu (Boys' Tennis), Srihari Ananthalwan (Boys' Tennis), Rushil Kagithala (Boys' Tennis), Vishvaa Ravishankar (Boys' Cross Country), Darius Whiteside (Boys' Football) and Riley Hayden (Girls' Golf). The students came up to receive a certificate and congratulations from the Board.

**TSD Mission Moment - National LitCon Conference Presenters.** The Board honored the 8 teachers who represented the Troy School District at LitCon, the National Reading Recovery/Early Literacy Conference, at the end of January. Literacy specialists Karen Bush and Holly Gordon presented "How Intentional Coaching Leads to Transformation." Literacy specialist Ashley Pellosmaa and ELD specialist Sue Reid, from Wattles, presented ways to collaborate in order to accelerate the multilingual learner in literacy. Classroom teachers Sara Provost, Alyssa Favot, Kristen Marcaccio and Erin Miller presented on how a deeper understanding of literacy processing theory helped them provide more responsive instruction in the classroom.

**Principal Appreciation Month - Resolution 23-017.** Noting that February has traditionally been celebrated statewide as Principal Appreciation Month, it was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Wilson to adopt a resolution reciting that energetic and inspiring school leadership is essential if teachers, schools and districts are to ensure that all Troy students are college and career ready; that K-12 school principals play a vital role in student success and act as liaison between the school and the community it serves; that Troy School District principals are dedicated, quality educational professionals; and that during this month the District joins educators, parents and students throughout Michigan to raise awareness of the importance of educational leadership. The resolution officially recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Mr. Schmidt offered a special thanks to the principals for their help in passing the bond and said the Board has appreciated their effort and support over the past six months.

**Additions & Deletions.** None. Mr. Schmidt moved the TCCHS student representative report up because Alexi had to leave early due to another obligation; Alexi Papadelis, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school.

**Public Communication (Agenda Items).** President Schmidt shared a statement providing the structure for the evening's public participation in compliance with the Open Meetings Act and reviewed the guidelines for public comment. Mrs. Tracy Owens, TSD parent, addressed the Board about the proposed changes to the High School Course Catalogue and the impact they will have on students. Mrs. Eleni Dilis, TSD parent, addressed the Board about honors classes being taken away and wanted parents to have a chance to share their thoughts on it.

**General - Consent Agenda, Resolution 23-018.** It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Board approve items A, B, C, D, E and F on the consent agenda: minutes of the January 10, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the January 17, 2023 Board of Education Organizational & Regular Meeting; Treasurer's Report - December 2022; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; and OCSBA Legislative Priorities and Bylaw Amendments. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Personnel.** None.

**Curriculum - High School Course Catalogue 2023-2024.** Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, and Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, shared a PowerPoint presentation and reported on the recommended changes to the 2023-2024 school year High School Course Catalogue. Resolution 23-019, moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne, resolved that the Board approves the proposed changes and adopts the 2023-2024 High School Course Description Book as presented. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Board discussion addressed the changes made to the catalogue and the high school courses offered, how different teaching is today from the old way of teaching, a style that allows students to own their learning, the importance of demonstrating the workshop model of teaching, changes in ELA and Chemistry courses, team sports, and that all physical education classes are co-ed.

**Business - Site Work Paving Projects, Resolution 23-020.** It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for the Site Work Paving Program be awarded to Nagle Paving in the amount printed in the minutes as $2,2,46,617.00 (rendered with an extra comma in the source), inclusive of a 6% contingency, and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund and Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Reports from Student Representatives to the Board.** Nish Palepu, student representative for Troy High School; Sara Ali, student representative for Athens High School; and Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, each shared reports on the events and activities at their schools.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items).** None. **Other.** None.

**Board Member Comments.** Dr. Philippart congratulated and thanked the principals for their work and dedication to the District and said she is impressed with the charity weeks in the high schools and proud of the spirit in the community and the caring students show. Mr. Haupt also commented on the charity events and how hard the students work for such a good cause. Mrs. Anne congratulated the Teacher of the Year nominees and winners and shared that she attended the Advocacy Conference in Washington, DC to advocate for the District's schools and students. Mrs. Alic spoke about the tragedy at Michigan State University and the students from Oxford now attending MSU having to live through something like this again. Mr. Hauff shared that the TSD supplement in the Troy Times is out. Dr. Wilson also mentioned the tragedy at MSU, commended principals, teachers and students for advocating for kids who need help, and congratulated students for raising so much money during charity week. Dr. Machesky thanked Mrs. Alic and Dr. Wilson for their comments on the tragedy in East Lansing, reported that bond work in the District continues with design meetings happening on a daily basis, congratulated the Teacher of the Year winners and nominees and invited the community to watch the video on the District website, and announced that March is Reading Month with teachers looking for guest readers. Mr. Schmidt described attending the Advocacy Institute in Washington and the five main issues addressed with representatives: funding that had been promised to schools years ago, expanding free lunches, expanding Title 1 funding, staffing shortages, and expanding the pilot program for electric busses. He gave a shout out to Kerry Birmingham for the Troy Times insert and commented on the tragedy at MSU.

**Announcements and adjournment.** Mr. Schmidt announced that the next Board Workshop would be held March 7th at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building, the Board Winter Retreat on Saturday, March 11th at 9:00 a.m. at the Administration Building, and the next Board Meeting on March 21st at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. The meeting adjourned at 8:35 p.m. Minutes respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (GH/jh).
